errors: c2 - c4 = 4.35 - (-7.33) = 11.68, but Gauss wrote 11.38. This propagates to 36.28 (should be 36.58) and 2.14 (should be 1.54). Hence a2 = 2.920 should be 2.933, a6 = 0.089 should be 0.064, and a10 = 0.103 should be 0.115.

Odd cosine block: the term labelled α+γ uses log 0.80956 = log 6.45, i.e. α alone. The correct value is α+γ = -6.45 + 2.93 = -3.52, giving a term of -0.1796 instead of -0.3291. Consequently the correct values are a1 ≈ -1.242 (Gauss -1.392), a5 ≈ 1.072 (0.923), a7 ≈ 0.469 (0.618) and a11 ≈ 0.080 (0.229).
δ = α-γ = -6.45 - 2.93 = -9.38, not -9.35. This is minor: a3 becomes ≈ -0.448 and a9 ≈ 0.245.
The log for the √3·d2 term is 0.97174, i.e. 9.37, whereas d2 = -9.35. The effect on a1, a5, a7, a11 is about 0.0014.
a8: (u0+u3) - (u1+u2) = 12.90 + 10.40 = +23.30, so a8 = +0.971. The page appears to show -23.30 and '-0.971 cos 8', an apparent sign slip (if the image is read correctly).

Data: x9 (135°) was taken as -0.85, but the mean of the previous page's values -0.7 and -0.0 is -0.35. This is either an averaging slip or a misreading of the previous page; the page's later sums use -0.85 consistently.
The sine coefficients b1..b11 are all correct given the data. The constants 1.14165 = log(24/√3), 1.29217 = log(48/√6), 1.22970 = log(24/√2) and 1.53073 = log(24√2) are correct.

results.what: 24-ordinate trigonometric (Fourier) analysis of circle-reading errors at 15° spacing, coefficients up to cos 12z, applied to instrument calibration (divided circle).
results.modern_name: Discrete Fourier transform / trigonometric interpolation (harmonic analysis of equally spaced data)
results.usually_credited_to: Clairaut, Lagrange (18th c.), Gauss (Theoria interpolationis, c.1805, publ. 1866), Bessel (1815-1828 in astronomical instrument work)

results.what: Successive symmetric folding (sums/differences x_j ± x_{N-j}, then ± about the quarter point) combined with grouped irrational factors √3/2, √2/2, √6/4 to reduce the 24-point DFT to a few multiplications.
results.modern_name: Symmetry-reduction scheme for the DFT (Runge's 12/24-ordinate schema; a radix-type reduction related to the FFT)
results.usually_credited_to: C. Runge (1903, 1905), with roots in Gauss's unpublished interpolation work (Heideman–Johnson–Burrus 1984)

deep.surprise_reason: This is a worked numerical application of trigonometric interpolation with a symmetric folding scheme, a method already known to be Gauss's from his Theoria interpolationis and his geodetic/astronomical calculations. The organized 24-ordinate folding anticipates Runge-style schemata, but Gauss's priority in efficient DFT computation is already documented. The value lies in documenting his instrument-error practice (and his arithmetic slips), not in a new result.
